doc.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022

title: Disappearing studios, file sharing and sculpting solos
summary: Studios have vanished; he now records at home with Ada, assembling solos from several takes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Has that scene — I won’t say disappeared — but

It’s disappeared in the fact that it’s all, you know what you see behind me. I’ve maybe done 500 sessions here at home with Ada or maybe I’ll add a part. But it’s all piecemeal. There are very few studios even in New York, there are only some small studios left. One by one all the studios that could actually house a whole group have fallen by the wayside. And everything now is just technology.
But you said — you’re pointing behind you and you’ve done 500 sessions, is that things that they send you the tracks?

Yeah. File sharing. And my wife is an expert at Pro Tools and editing and we sit here and if I’m lucky or if she’s lucky we’ll get a solo, one or two takes. But more often than not we sculpt solos for records. You know we’ll sculpt a solo. I’ll play five takes and we’ll put together something that sounds kind of perfect to us. That’s what they call for, really.
And that’s what sculpt means? The term sculpt?

We sculpt a solo from maybe five different takes. It has to sit right in a track you know or maybe I hold a note too long so we shorten the note alter electronically or the pitch is a little out so we’ll change — I mean it’s not optimal by any stretch of the imagination. I miss those days when we’re all in the studio — at least the horn sections — so it was a lot of overdubbing. Then even during the busy days, well in the first few years you were. When I first started doing studio work they would actually have sessions with everyone in there at the same time. But then four tracks led to eight tracks and then it was better, it was more optimal just to have the rhythm section, call the horns, call the strings later.
